extracted.intended_audience: public commenters, administrative advocates, and legal scholars drafting regulatory comments
extracted.subtask_description: Using Sunstein's interpretive norms to craft notice-and-comment submissions that promote agency deliberation, counter factional capture, and protect disadvantaged groups by grounding arguments in public-regarding statutory purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote agency deliberation
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments are valuable when they promote agency deliberation rather than substitute preference-aggregation for reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A high-quality comment provides reasons connected to public values, engages the agency's reasoning rather than asserting raw preferences, and surfaces tradeoffs the agency must reason through.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serve as a deliberative supplement when deliberation is absent
rubrics_metrics.description: When deliberation is captured or thin, comments can serve as a deliberative supplement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective comments articulate the public interest beyond narrow stakeholder positions, bring perspectives systematically excluded from agency deliberation, and apply public-regarding reasoning to private interest claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit factionalism and expose self-interested representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and counteract narrow factional or captured analysis in the rulemaking record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective comments identify when industry submissions reflect captured analysis, trace stakeholder positions to their underlying interests, and argue against rules that disproportionately benefit the most concentrated interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote political equality and protect disadvantaged groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Give priority to identifying and addressing harms to disadvantaged or vulnerable populations in regulatory action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective comments identify distributional impacts on disadvantaged populations, argue against rules that systematically harm vulnerable groups, and bring affected disadvantaged voices to the docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide reasons connected to public values
rubrics_metrics.description: Ground arguments in public-regarding values rather than mere expression of private preferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid asserting raw preferences; instead connect critiques or suggestions to public values and how they further statutory purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage the agency's reasoning (not just preferences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Directly engage and challenge the agency's stated reasons and analysis rather than only stating policy preferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pinpoint flaws or omissions in the agency's reasoning, show relevant counter-evidence or arguments, and explain implications for the agency's legal or policy analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surface tradeoffs the agency must reason through
rubrics_metrics.description: Make explicit the competing considerations and consequences that the agency should weigh.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Help the agency see the relevant tradeoffs (e.g., costs vs. benefits, distributional effects) so deliberation is substantive rather than rhetorical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Articulate the public interest beyond narrow stakeholder positions
rubrics_metrics.description: Represent broader public-regarding concerns when stakeholder input is one-sided or dominated by concentrated interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the public interest differs from particularized private interests and provide evidence or reasoning supporting that broader perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trace stakeholder positions to underlying interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Expose the interests and incentives that produce particular stakeholder submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Showing the link between a party's position and its concentrated interests helps illuminate potential bias and the limits of relying on that submission as representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify distributional consequences on disadvantaged populations
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess and highlight how a proposed rule or policy will affect different groups, especially vulnerable or disadvantaged populations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence, data, or argumentation about disparate impacts and argue for mitigating measures or alternative approaches when harms are identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground reasoning in public values and statutory purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Connect comment arguments to public-regarding statutory purposes and avoid relying solely on private-interest rationales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should link claims to the statute's text and purposes; the author cautions that importing extra-statutory values without textual hooks risks critique—so engage the statutory language explicitly.
